Commentary.Commentary: The action is set to resume. Devon Conway stands nears the crease and does some shadow batting before he is joined by his opening partner in Tom Latham. James Anderson meanwhile is seen doing some final bandwork near the ropes. The two umpires head out with the new cherry and the Kiwis openers follow. Soon the English players take the field as well. It will be the veteran James Anderson to start with the new ball.
... THIRD INNINGS ...

It was a one-man show in the opening moments of the morning session as Tim Southee who came in with an overnight score 23 runs headed back to the dressing room on 73 runs off just 49 balls. New Zealand needed 236 to avoid the follow-on but they could not get a small victory in this innings. For England, it was Stuart Broad who stood out with the ball this morning, as he took the remaining three wickets to put his side in a solid position. Overall, it was a great bowling display from England. New Zealand now have another opportunity here to get back into the game if they get off to a solid start with the bat. Do join us shortly for the third innings.

Phew! What an entertaining affair it has been in the morning session of the Moving Day. England though come out on top undoubtedly as they bundle out New Zealand at 209 and they have enforced the follow-on here. New Zealand still trail by 226 runs.

OUT! TAKEN! Stuart Broad gets the last wicket! That is it for New Zealand ad they have been bowled out for 209. Broad lands this back of a length and on middle, angling in with extra bounce, Matt Henry gets hurried and is in a awkward position to defend, and the ball takes the outside edge and lobs up in the air towards gully where James Anderson takes a dolly.
Commentary.Howout: c James Anderson b Stuart Broad

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Matt Henry steers it towards point, Neil Wagner wants the run and is halfway down the pitch, but Henry is not interested.
Flatter, outside off. Neil Wagner dabs it to the off side.
On off, blocked on the front foot.
It is tossed up, around off. Neil Wagner goes for the reverse sweep but misses it completely. He wears it on his pads. Leach appeals but the umpire is unmoved.
Floats it up, on off. blocked to point.
Fuller, on leg. Henry clips it through mid-wicket for one.
Full and on off. Henry drives it uppishly to the right of extra covers.
Length, on off. Neil Wagner blocks it to covers.
Neil Wagner is the last man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tom Blundell holes out this time. It is a short ball, on off. Tom Blundell steps out of the crease and goes for the pull shot. He does not middle it and goes low and straight towards mid on. Jack Leach stationed there takes a sharp low catch by getting down on his knees.
Commentary.Howout: c Jack Leach b Stuart Broad

Commentary.Commentary: It is full, on fifth stump. Tom Blundell leans in and pushes it gently to covers.
On a length, outside off. Matt Henry upper cuts it down to third man and gets to the other end.
A sharp bouncer, on off. Matt Henry tries to hook it away but misses.
FOUR! Matt Henry is off the mark with a boundary. It is a short ball, on off. Matt Henry gets inside the line and flicks it down to fine leg. A couple of bounces over the ropes.

Tom Blundell dances down the track to this full ball. He drills it back to the bowler. Jack Leach does well to make a half-stop and save a single here. An opportunity for England to attack the new batter in Henry.
Flatter, outside off. Tom Blundell eases it to backward point.
On off, tapped to the off side.
Leach drifts it in, around off. It turns away with some extra bounce. Tom Blundell gets beaten on the outside edge as he tries to cut it away.
Short, outside off. Tom Blundell cuts it past backward point. He pushes hard for the first one and comes back for the second.
Fuller, in-line with the stumps. Tom Blundell steps down the wicket and blocks it solidly.
Change of ends for Jack Leach.
Short one, on middle and leg. Matt Henry sways away from the line of the delivery here.
A bumper down leg, left alone.
Length ball, on the pads. Matt Henry flicks it to the leg side.
Matt Henry comes out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tim Southee's entertaining innings comes to an end. It is full-length ball, on leg stump. Tim Southee goes for the flick but is a bit early into his shot. The ball takes the leading edge and lobs towards mid-wicket. Zak Crawley gets enough time to settle himself and takes a dolly here. New Zealand need 35 more runs to avoid follow-on.
Commentary.Howout: c Zak Crawley b Stuart Broad

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! And 200 up for New Zealand. It is a short ball, on off. Tim Southee tries to heave it across the line but it catches the top-edge. The ball goes way high in the air towards fine leg. Jack Leach gets to his right, settles under it but does not hold on to it. The batters take a couple.

FOUR! Up and over! It does not matter who comes into the attack. Tim Southee is speaking only one language here. It is a good-length ball, on middle. Tim Southee clears his front leg and slaps it over mid off for four runs.
Stuart Broad replaces Jack Leach.
Full, angled into the pads. Tom Blundell tucks it to mid-wicket.
On a length, outside off, jags back in a touch. Tom Blundell makes a good leave.
Good length, sliding down leg. Tim Southee flicks it down to fine leg and crosses.
SIX! Fireworks going on in Wellington. A short ball, on leg. Tim Southee swivels and hooks it over the square leg fence for a maximum.
A sharp bouncer, on the body. Tim Southee sways away from the line here.
Length and on top of off. Tim Southee opens the face late and guides it to backward point.
A single now as this full ball is tapped to the off side.

SIX! Tim Southee cannot do anything wrong with the bat this morning. It is looped up, outside off. Tim Southee gets down on one knee to smack it flat and hard over the long on fence. The umpire is being made to do some exercise in this over.
Full and on off, dabbed to the off side.
Halt! The ball is stuck on the roof with that previous shot from Tim Southee. The umpires take out another ball from the box.

SIX! BANG! What a knock this is turning out to be from Tim Southee. He is certainly playing a captain's knock here. It is tossed up, full and on off. Tim Southee makes good use of the feet once again and dispatches it over the bowler's head for a biggie. He gets if half-ton in fine fashion. To be honest, Tim Southee is using his feet more than any top-orders for the Kiwis.
Shorter,outside off, turning away a bit. Tim Southee rocks back and tries to cut it away but misses. He gets beaten on the outside edge.
SIX! High and handsome! It is full, wide outside off. Tim Southee uses his feet and smokes it over the long on fence.
FOUR! Wonderful shot! It is pitched up, on fourth stump. Tom Blundell lunges and creams it through cover for four runs. He couldn't have hit it any better.
Outside off, left alone.

Ollie Robinson fires it full, on middle and leg. Tim Southee shuffles and tries to flick it away. He gets some bat on it, although Ollie Robinson thinks it has hit his pads. Ben Stokes takes the review but the UltraEdge confirms that the bat is involved.
Is that out? England have taken a review for a LBW decision on Tim Southee. UltraEdge shows that Southee has hit the bat and on-field call of Not Out will remain.
A single now as Tom Blundell punches this length ball to the off side.

Woah! Natural variation this time. It is a length ball, that nips in from outside off. Although it stays low off the deck. Tom Blundell gets beaten on the inside edge but is fortunate to see the ball go through to the keeper.
Robinson goes full and on off. Blundell knocks it to covers.
On off, blocked to the off side.
NO BALL! Jack Leach has to reload the final delivery. Full and on off, defended solidly.
Full and on leg, defended out.
A bit short, turning away with some bounce. Tom Blundell goes back and punches it past extra covers for one more.
Tim Southee now rotates the striker as he nudges this full ball to the leg side. This is good running.
Short, outside off. Tom Blundell cuts it hard to sweeper cover for one.
Floats it up, full and on off. Tom Blundell prods and blocks it into the deck.

Ollie Robinson dishes a well-directed bouncer, on leg stump. Tim Southee goes back and tries to hook it away. He gets no connection here. The ball pings the helmet on its way to the keeper. There is a stifled appeal but the umpire is unmoved.
Bit fuller, on off. Southee drives it to extra cover, but could not find the gap this time.
Good length, wide of off. Tim Southee goes after it but misses.
FOUR! Tim Southee is scoring runs for fun here. It is a short ball, outside off. Tim Southee steps down and slaps it over covers for a cracking boundary.
Length and on off, blocked away.

So close! It is much fuller, on fourth stump. Tim Southee tries to go downtown but misses it by a mile, although the ball whizzes past the off pole here. Tim Southee has some ladyluck on his side here.
On  off, Tom Blundell eases it to the off side.
A single now as this is tapped to point.
FOUR! Much better shot. No chance for any fielder this time. Tim Southee uses his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and smacks it over the bowler's head for four runs.
Looped up, around off, Tim Southee blocks it out.

FOUR! Incredible effort from Ben Stokes. This could have been a stunning catch. Ben Stokes commits to this catch but it goes down in vain and to rub salt on the wounds, it rolls over the ropes. It is full and on off. Tim Southee dances down the track, gets under it and lofts it high towards long on. Ben Stokes runs backwards from mid on. He gives it a long chase, dives forward, although the ball does not stick in his palms and it goes for four.
This is flat, attaking the stumps. Tim Southee blocks it out firmly.
England going with spin straightaway as Jack Leach is ready to share the attack.
A length ball, around off. Tom Blundell blocks it out watchfully. 10 runs off the first over. A positive start for the Kiwis.
Outside off, Tom Blundell leaves it alone for the keeper.
FOUR! This is a picturesque shot! Robinson pitches it up, outside off. Tom Blundell leans in and creams it through the cover region for a boundary.

EDGED! It is a length ball, in the channel. Tom Blundell tries to block it away but gets a thick outside edge. Fortunately, he plays it with soft hands and the ball just lands short of Harry Brook in the slip cordon.
Nicely bowled! On a length, drifts in, on fourth stump, it straightens a touch off the deck. Tom Blundell comes forward and tries to defend it out but gets beaten on the outside edge.

Robinson now delivers it on a length, on fourth stump. Tim Southee stays back and punches it through the gap at covers. The batters take three runs before Stuart Broad cuts it out. First runs of the morning for New Zealand.

Ollie Robinson starts with a bouncer, on off. This one flies off the deck. Tim Southee gets on his toes and blocks it off the top half of the blade. The umpire signals a no ball as the bowler oversteps.

We are all set for the start of Day 3! England players are making their way out in the middle now. Tim Southee and Tom Blundell to fight for New Zealand to save follow-on. Ollie Robinson to start the proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

New Zealand trail by 297 runs with only three wickets remaining. Tim Southee and Tom Blundell are at the crease, and this pair is their last hope if they are to avoid the follow-on, but that looks like an uphill task at the moment. England, on the other hand, have outplayed the Kiwis in all departments, and James Anderson showed why he is the top-ranked bowler in Tests, and that too at the age of 40. Jack Leach supported him well, and their aim will be to bowl out New Zealand as soon as possible and then maybe ask them to bat again to finish them off and seal the series. Stay tuned for all the action on Day 3 starting in a bit.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! The start of Day 3 of the second Test between New Zealand and England is not too far away and we know that Day 3 is also known as Moving Day and we could be getting a result here if weather permits. The rain has cost us a lot of overs till now, but England have still managed to be in spot from where losing would be harder than to win. The Kiwis will hope that something miraculous happens and they get back into this game.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from Day 2 of this Test match, and it was another exciting Day of Test cricket that ended early because of rain again. England are well ahead in this one, and with weather conditions like this, they might look to force the follow-on. Day 3 is known as the Moving Day and we will surely get close to a result if rain permits. The action will begin early to cover up the lost overs, so the first ball will be bowled at 3 am IST (9.30 pm GMT, Previous Day). Do join us for the build-up. Until then, Cheers and Goodbye!

New Zealand, just like on Day 1 were able to pick up a few quick wickets early on and it was Matt Henry again who started proceedings for them by getting rid of Harry Brook quite early. They picked up wickets at regular intervals, but also leaked runs which did not help them in any way. Henry was their best bowler with four wickets. They came out to bat trailing by 435 runs, and things got from bad to worse for them as they lost Kane Williamson, Devon Conway and Will Young in quick succession and were reduced to 21-3 exactly like England. Tom Latham and Henry Nicholls steadied their ship for a bit, but Latham got dismissed with a controversial decision which started a mini collapse for them and they found themselves at 103-7. However, then their skipper, Tim Southee came out to bat and played a few lusty blows and provided support to Tom Blundell who is their last recognised batter. Just as they were looking good and started scoring runs at a brisk rate, rain played spoilsport and now they will have to keep their focus and continue on Day 3.

Despite losing a few wickets in early on, England did not let their scoring rate decrease. Harry Brook would have been disappointed as he missed out on his double hundred, but Joe Root led the charge for his team with a couple of cameos from Ben Stokes and Ollie Robinson. Root reached his 150 and  Stokes decided to declare the innings at 435/8. They continued their momentum with the ball as well as James Anderson provided them with two crucial breakthroughs in no time before Lunch. In the second session, Anderson once again got a wicket, but then it was all about Jack Leach who  troubled the Kiwi batters and ran through their middle order picking up three wickets which included the dismissal of two set batters in Henry Nicholls and Tom Latham. Stuart Broad also got into the act and picked up a wicket. However, after just nine overs in the third session, the drizzle started and no more play was possible.

That will be Stumps on Day 2! The consistent rain meant that we could not get any further play. New Zealand still trail by 297 runs with three wickets in hand. A total of 258 runs were scored and 12 wickets fell on Day 2. However, England would be a bit disappointed as they would have liked to bowl the Kiwis out here, but they will have to wait now. New Zealand, on the other hand needs a miracle to avoid the follow-on, and they will hope that someone stands up for them.

Update 9.37 am IST (4.07 am GMT) - Good news folks! The covers are off now and the umpires walk out to have an inspection. The word from the middle is that the game will resume at 9.45 am IST (4.15 GMT). Join us for all the action. OH NO!! Just when the umpires were done with the inspection. The drizzle is back and the covers are on as well. The groundstaff could not even leave the field after taking the covers off. The wait game resets here.

Update 9.15 am IST (3.45 am GMT) - Oh..no! The rain has started now. Both the umpires have a chat and asks the players to go off field now. The covers are coming on, but it is a slight drizzle and we can hope for further action. Stay with us.
Broad goes full, on fifth stump. Tom Blundell steps across and blocks it under his eyes. New Zealand trail by 297 runs.
Length, in the channel. Tim Southee gets it to cover off the outer half. They take a single.
Back of a length, outside off, shaping further away. Tim Southee looks to cut it away but misses and gets beaten on the outside edge.
It is very full, on fourth stump. Tim Southee goes back and jams it back to the bowler. Broad is quick to get low and stop the ball.
Broad fires it full, down leg. Tom Blundell stays inside the crease and wrists it gently to mid-wicket for one more.
A length ball, outside off, it jags back in a touch. Tim Southee tries to flick it to the leg side but is a bit early into his shot. The ball goes to covers off his fingers. One taken.
FOUR! Sweet timing! It is short, in the channel. Tom Blundell gets on his back and cuts it hard and flat through point. The ball races away to the fence.
Flatter, outside off. Tom Blundell plays it late to Joe Root at first slip.
On off, defended out.
Flatter and on middle. Tom Blundell goes back and tries to pull it away. It rolls out to the leg side off the inside edge.
Much fuller, around off. Tom Blundell defends it into the deck.
Full and on middle. Tom Blundell blocks it on his front foot.
A bit slower, full and on off. Tim Southee shuffles and tucks it to the leg side. 11 runs off the over. The skipper is turning on the heat with the bat in hand here.
SIX! Tim Southee is making his intent clear. It is short, on middle. Tim Southee makes some room and launches it over the cow corner fence for a biggie.

FOUR! EDGY! Some lucky finally on New Zealand's side. It is a short ball, outside off. Tim Southee stands tall and heaves across the line. The ball catches the top-edge, flies over the keeper's head for four runs. It certainly does not matter how the runs come now.
Full length, drifting down leg. Tom Blundell clips it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Broad goes a bit fuller this time, swinging in on off. Tom Blundell fends it out to the off side.
On a length, outside off, nips back in off the deck. Tom Blundell gets forward to block it out firmly.
Full and on off. Southee dabs it to silly point, on a bounce though. Just a couple of the over.
Leach serves it full, sliding down leg. Tim Southee tickles it down to fine leg for a brace.
On off, defended out solidly.
Tosses it up, full, on off. Tim Southee presses forward and gets it to point off the outer half.
Full and on off. Tim Southee gets forward and blocks it back to the bowler.
Shortish, outside off. Tim Southee stays back and punches it to cover.
Length again and on middle, Tom Blundell pats it back towards the bowler.
Pulls his length back a bit, on off, Tom Blundell pushes it towards short covers. There is a bit of hesitation between the batters, but no harm done in the end.
Goes fuller this time, on off, Tom Blundell lets it go to the keeper.
On a length and on off, Tim Southee taps it in front of point for a single.
Touch fuller and on off, Tim Southee heaves it towards mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right to stop it.
SIX! BANG! Tim Southee goes big now! This is on a good length and on middle, Tim Southee clears his front leg and slogs it over the wide long on fence for a biggie.
FOUR! Powered away! This is short and around off, Tom Blundell makes some room and smashes it over mid on for a boundary.
Darts this one full and on middle, Tim Southee nudges it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Floated, full and on off, Tom Blundell drives it towards long off for a single.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Tom Blundell leans on and blocks it out.
Short again and on off, Tom Blundell pushes it towards short covers.
Flatter, short and on middle, Tom Blundell makes room and punches it towards point.
Pitched up, on off, Tom Blundell drives it wide of point where the fielder dives to his right to stop it. They cross.
This is on a hard length and on off, angling in, Tom Blundell makes an easy leave.
Full and on off, Tim Southee knocks it to the left of short covers for a quick single.
Tim Southee is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Stuart Broad finally gets a wicket! He lands this on a hard length and around off, angling in, Michael Bracewell is anticipating a fuller length and is early into his defensive shot, and the ball lobs up off the bat towards the bowler where Stuart Broad takes a dolly. He cannot believe his luck while Bracewell stands there in disbelief as well. New Zealand in huge trouble as they are seven down now!
Back of a length and outside off, Michael Bracewell leaves it alone.
This is on a good length and on off, Michael Bracewell turns it towards short mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and on off, Tom Blundell blocks it towards silly point.
Floated, full and on middle, Tom Blundell defends it on the front foot.
Shortish and around leg, Michael Bracewell heaves it towards deep backward square leg for a single.
FOUR! Good shot! This is tossed up, full and on leg, Michael Bracewell goes down and nails his sweep towards the deep backward square leg fence for a boundary.
Short again and on leg, Michael Bracewell turns it towards backward short leg.
Quicker, short and on leg, Michael Bracewell moves back and flicks it towards square leg.
Jack Leach to bowl from the other end.
A bit fuller and on middle, Tom Blundell defends it out with the inner half of his bat.
Short of a length and on leg, Michael Bracewell clips it towards deep square leg for a run and gets off the mark.
Goes full and on middle, angling in, Michael Bracewell tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
On a length and on off, Tom Blundell pushes it wide of short covers for a quick single.
Back of a length and on off, angling in, Tom Blundell keeps it out towards short covers.
This is on a good length and on middle, Tom Blundell nudges it towards mid-wicket.
We are back for the third session! The players are making their way out in the middle now. Michael Bracewell joins Tom Blundell at the crease. Stuart Broad to start proceedings with the ball.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Phew! This session went at a rate of knots. New Zealand have lost 6 wickets with just 96 runs on the board. Ollie Pope is delighted as he walks off the field now. England couldn't have asked for a better way to head into the Tea break. James Anderson was the one who started the proceedings in the post-Lunch session by getting rid of Will Young. Then, Jack Leach came to the fore and spun a web around the batters and picked up three wickets in no time to put the Kiwis in a precarious position. Only a miracle now can get the Kiwis back into the game here. New Zealand are behind by 339 runs and they certainly have their task cut out. New Zealand haven't been able to build solid stands in the middle and that is the difference between the two sides here. The final session on Day 2 will begin at 8.30 am IST (3 am GMT). Do join us to find out if New Zealand have any fight left in them.

OUT! TAKEN! A splendid catch to get rid of Daryl Mitchell! New Zealand lose a wicket on the last ball of the second session. Jack Leach gives this one some air, on off, Daryl Mitchell prods forward to defend, but is a bit early into his shot, and rather than hitting the ball, the ball hit his bat and loops up in the air, Ollie Pope at silly point shows great reflexes and grabs it with his outstreched right hand. England players celebrate, but Daryl Mitchell will be kicking himself. New Zealand six down now! THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 2!
Commentary.Howout: c Ollie Pope b Jack Leach

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, blocked out.
Flighted, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell knocks it back to the bowler.
Short and on middle, Tom Blundell tucks it through mid-wicket for one.
Floated, full and on off, Daryl Mitchell works it with the inner half towards square leg for a single.
Tossed up, full and on off, Daryl Mitchell blocks it out.
Pitched up, on middle, Daryl Mitchell glances it towards the vacant deep mid-wicket region where the ball stops due to the slow outfield. Three runs taken!
Overpitched and on off, Daryl Mitchell is solid in his defense again.
Length again and on middle, Tom Blundell tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Pulls his length back a bit, on middle, Tom Blundell pushes it towards short covers.
Fuller one and on off, Tom Blundell drives it firmly, but the fielder at short covers dives to his right to stop it.
On a length and on off, Tom Blundell knocks it towards short covers.
Flatter, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell works it with the inner half towards square leg.
Gives this one some air, on off, Daryl Mitchell blocks it out.
Short again and on off, Daryl Mitchell pushes it, but it hits the fielder at silly point and goes nowhere.
Slightly shorter and on off, Tom Blundell forces it wide of mid off for a single.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Tom Blundell blocks it to the leg side.
Short and on middle, Tom Blundell moves back and punches it towards short covers.
Full again and on middle, Tom Blundell drives it towards short mid on where a fumble allows a run.
Touch fuller and on off, Tom Blundell offers no shot at it.
This is on a good length and on off, Tom Blundell knocks it towards covers.
Back of a length and on leg, Daryl Mitchell nudges it towards square leg for a single.
On a length and on off, nips back in, Daryl Mitchell leaves it alone.
Full and on off, Tom Blundell pushes it towards covers for a single.
Ripper! This is floated, on off, grips and turns away sharply, Daryl Mitchell is beateon on the outside edge as he tries to defend.
Slower through the air, on off, Daryl Mitchell fends it to the right of silly point.
Flighted, full and on leg, Daryl Mitchell flicks it uppishly but wide of short mid-wicket for a brace.
Gives this one some air, on middle, turning away, Daryl Mitchell moves back and keeps it down to the off side.
Floated, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell defends it down the pitch.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell leans on and blocks it to the right of the bowler.
Back of a length and on off, Tom Blundell steers it towards point.
Goes a bit fuller and on off, shaping in, Tom Blundell makes another good leave.
Length again and on middle, angling in, Tom Blundell tries to fend it away, but gets a bottom edge onto his pads as the ball goes nowhere.
On a length and on middle, Tom Blundell blocks it down the pitch.
FOUR! Nice shot! James Anderson serves this full and on off, Tom Blundell stays there and drives it firmly towards the vacant long off fence for a boundary.
This is on a hard length and on middle, angling in, Tom Blundell looks to work it away, but misses and gets hit high on his body.
James Anderson (7-1-26-3) is back on.
A maiden over! This is flatter and outside off, Daryl Mitchell leaves it alone.
A bit short and on off, Daryl Mitchell moves back and punches it towards covers.
On middle, blocked out.
Flighted, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell defends it on the front foot.
Floated and on middle, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet to knock it towards short mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his left to stop the single.
Tossed up, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell leans on and blocks it out.
Ollie Robinson lands this on a hard length and outside off, shaping away, Tom Blundell offers no shot at it.
Length again and around off, Tom Blundell steers it through point for a couple of runs.
Pulls his length back a bit, on middle, Tom Blundell defends it to the leg side.
Goes fuller and on middle, Tom Blundell drills it towards short mid-wicket.
This is on a good length and on off, angling in sharply, Tom Blundell lets it got to the keeper. Good leave!
Full and outside off, Tom Blundell prods forward and leaves it alone.
Flatter and on middle. Tom Blundell goes back and nudges it to the leg side for one. He gets off the mark here.
On off, blocked out.
Flights it up, on off. It grips and turns away off the deck, Tom Blundell tries to go after it but misses. The ball zips past the outside edge.
On middle and leg, tucked away to the leg side.
Tom Blundell is the next man in with New Zealand in a spot of bother.

OUT! CAUGHT! New Zealand now have half of their side sent back to the hut. A horrible dismissal here. Jack Leach gets his second wicket in no time. It is tossed up, around middle. Henry Nicholls switches his stance and goes for the reverse sweep. It brushes his gloves and pops up. The ball goes to the left of short leg. Ollie Pope dives that side and takes a stunning one-handed catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Ollie Pope b Jack Leach

Commentary.Commentary: Slower through the air, full and on off. Henry Nicholls nudges it towards mid-wicket.
Ollie Robinson serves a length ball, outside off. It jabs back in with some extra bounce. Daryl Mitchell shoulders his arms at it and takes a blow near the stomach area.
Swing and a miss! Ollie Robinson serves a length ball, wide of off. Daryl Mitchell comes across a long way to defend it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
On a length, in the channel. Daryl Mitchell presses forward and defends it to covers.
Too full and straight, around off. Daryl Mitchell helps it back to the bowler.
Length, on sixth stump. Daryl Mitchell shuffles and defends it to cover.
Robinson starts this over with a full one, outside off. Daryl Mitchell tries to punch it through the line but gets it to square leg off the inside edge. The batters take a couple.
On off, Henry Nicholls blocks it out solidly.
FOUR! Top shot! Second boundary of the over. Jack Leach goes full, on middle. Henry Nicholls prods and the broom comes out once again. Nicholls sweeps it behind square for another boundary.
Flatter and on off. Henry Nicholls goes back and knocks it towards mid on.
Fuller, on the pads. Henry Nicholls nudges it to the leg side.
FOUR! Nicely played! Jack Leach goes full once again, outside off. Henry Nicholls gets down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
It is full and outside off. Henry Nicholls gets low and sweeps it to the right of short third man. The batters take two runs.
On a good length, on fifth stump, jabs back in late. Daryl Mitchell shuffles and makes a good leave.
Length, outside off, left alone.

Ollie Robinson dishes a length ball, outside off. It nips in off the deck. Daryl Mitchell presses forward and tries to defend it out. He gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The ball pops up but does not carry towards the keeper.
Much fuller, outside off. Daryl Mitchell gets forward and blocks it to mid off.
It is a length ball, on off. Daryl Mitchell shuffles and blocks it out.
On a length and on middle, Henry Nicholls nudges it towards square leg for a single.
Flighted, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell leans on and nudges it to the leg side.
Quicker, short and on middle, Daryl Mitchell moves back and blocks it out.
Slowr through the air, on off, turning away, Daryl Mitchell fends it to the off side.
FOUR! Daryl Mitchell gets off the mark in style! This is floated, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and drives it past the bowler for a boundary.
Daryl Mitchell walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Matter of inches here. Tom Latham is extremely gutted as he trudges back to the dressing room. Some 'boos' can be heard from the crowd as well. The fans are not holding themselves back here from expressing their feelings. It is tossed up, around off. Tom Latham goes for the reverse sweep but misses. The ball lobs off his gloves and Joe Root takes a dolly at first slip. An appeal is made and up goes the dreaded finger. Tom Latham though takes the review instantly. He thinks that iths comes off his arm guard. The third umpire goes through the replays several times. In the front-on vision it looks like it comes arm guard first, although, the side-on angle shows that the ball first comes in contact with the top of the glove. The third umpire asks the on-field umpire to stick with the original decision.
Commentary.Howout: c Joe Root b Jack Leach

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, around off, turning in. Tom Latham clips it to the leg side.

Drinks! New Zealand lost their top order for not much early on. However, Tom Latham and Henry Nicholls has taken them out of trouble, but they know that this will need to continuw if they want to get near the England total. England will be happy with how things are going with James Anderson leading from the front. They will hope to get a couple of breakthroughs in this session to put more pressure on the Kiwis.
Robinson serves it full, on fifth stump. Henry Nicholls shuffles across to defend it out. Just a single run off it.
It is full, on off. Henry Nicholls presses forward  and defends it out solidly.
Outside off, left alone.
Robinson dishes a length ball, around off. It nips in off the deck. Henry Nicholls tries to flick it away but gets pinged on his pads. A stifled appeal but the umpire shows no interest.
It is full, angled into the pads. Tom Latham hangs back and flicks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Ollie Robinson pitches it up, full and on off. Tom Latham dabs it out to the off side.
A bit short, on middle and leg. Tom Latham flicks it to square leg for a single.
SIX! BANG! Jack Leach goes full and on off. Tom Latham dances down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and smokes it over the bowler's head for a maximum.
On the pads, tucked past Ollie Pope on the leg side.
Much better connection! Tossed up, full and outside off. Henry Nicholls gets low and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for one.

Shouts of 'catch it'! It is looped up, around off, with some extra bounce off the deck. Henry Nicholls prods and tries to sweep it away. He misses, although it lobs off his arms and lands short of the man at leg slip.
Floats it up, full and outside off. Henry Nicholls presses forward and blocks.
We will see some spin now as Jack Leach is ready to bowl.
A length ball, in the channel. Tom Latham gets on his front foot and defends it back to the bowler.
On off, blocked out solidly.
Ollie Robinson dishes a length ball, on off. Tom Latham flicks it to the right of short leg. Ollie Pope is quick to react. He dives to his right and makes a sharp stop.
Length and on off, blocked out.
BEATEN! Ollie Robinson now serves it on a length, outside off. It nips away off the deck. Tom Latham tries to defend it out but gets beaten on the outside edge.

Close! It is a length ball, that lands outside off and shapes in off the deck. Although, the bounce takes it over the stumps. Tom Latham makes a good leave here. Ollie Robinson cannot believe how has this not hit the stumps.
Broad dishes a full ball, outside off. Tom Latham gets on his front foot and punches it through the gap at covers. The batters take three runs before the fielder cuts it off.
Broad goes full, outside off. Tom Latham lets it be.
Outside off, left alone.
On a length, on fifth stump. Tom Latham get forward and dabs it out to safety.
Much fuller, angled in around off. Tom Latham closes the face and tucks it to the leg side.
Shortish, around off. Henry Nicholls charges down the wicket and flicks it towards mid-wicket. One taken.
Much fuller, outside off, shaping away off the deck. Tom Latham has no shot to offer. Third consecutive maiden for Ollie Robinson.
Good leave! It is a length ball, that lands around middle and nips away a touch. Tom Latham trusts the bounce here and shoulders his arms at it.
Make that four! Ollie Robinson now changes the angle as he comes from over the wicket. It is on a good-length, angling across the left-hander. Left alone.
Three dots in a row! It is full, angled into the pads. Tom Latham blocks it to the leg side off the inner half.
It is much fuller, on off. Tom Latham gets on his front foot and blocks it back to the bowler off the toe end.
Ollie Robinson comes from 'round the wicket. It is a length ball, angled in around off. Tom Latham defends it out solidly.
This is on a hard length and on middle, Henry Nicholls keeps it out to the leg side.
Goes back to his fuller length, on middle, angling in, Henry Nicholls fends it to the left of the bowler.
On a length and on middle, angling in, Henry Nicholls looks to block it, but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is a slight appeal for LBW, but turned down.
Overpiched and on off, Tom Latham drives it towards covers for a single.
Another yorker, on middle, Tom Latham jams it out towards short mid-wicket.
Stuart Broad nails the yorker, on off, angling in, Tom Latham digs it out back towards the bowler.
Back of a length and around off, Henry Nicholls moves across and has a nibble at it, but gets beaten on the outside edge due to the extra bounce.
Fuller once more, on middle, angling in, Henry Nicholls knocks it back to the bowler.
Goes a bit fuller and on off, angling away again, Henry Nicholls lets it go to the keeper.
Length again and on the sixth stump line, angling away, Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
On a length and around leg, Henry Nicholls keeps it out down the pitch.
Ollie Robinson begins with a pitched-up delivery, on middle, Henry Nicholls works it towards short mid-wicket.
Change. Ollie Robinson now comes into the attack. He has bowled a single over so far.
This is on a good length and on off, straightens after hitting the deck, Tom Latham looks to play at it, but gets beaten on the outside edge.
On a length and on leg, Henry Nicholls nudges it towards fine leg for a single.
Overpitched and around off, Tom Latham drills it through covers as Ben Duckett chases it. The batters take on the arm and completes three runs.
Fuller once more, on middle, Tom Latham blocks it back to the bowler.
Full again and on leg, Tom Latham turns it towards short mid-wicket.
Full and on off, Henry Nicholls pushes it to the right of short covers for a single.
Stuart Broad continues with the fuller length, on leg this time, Henry Nicholls tucks it through mid-wicket for three runs.
Pitched up, on off, Tom Latham works it with the outer half through point for a single.
Full again and on middle, angling in, Tom Latham misses his flick and gets hit on the thigh pads.
Touch fuller, outside off, shaping away, Tom Latham lets it go to the keeper.
Length again and outside off, Tom Latham shoulders arms to it.
EDGED AND FOUR! This is on a good length and on off, angling in, Tom Latham looks to fend it, but gets an outside edge on the bounce and between gully and third slip for a boundary.
A bit fuller and on off, Henry Nicholls pushes it towards covers.
FOUR! Nice timing! This on a hard length and around leg, Henry Nicholls flicks it with great timing towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Length again, on middle, Henry Nicholls misses his flick and gets hit high on his body.
Pulls his length back a bit, on leg, Henry Nicholls tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Good shot! James Anderson serves this full and on middle, Henry Nicholls stays there and drives it towards the vacant long on fence for a boundary.
This is on a good length and on leg, Henry Nicholls nudges it towards short fine leg.
Touch fuller and outside off, Tom Latham leaves it alone.
On a length and on off, Tom Latham dabs it towards gully.
Back of a length and around off, shaping away again, Tom Latham is in two mind whether to play it or not, and withdraws his bat at the last moment.
This is on a hard length and outside off, shaping furhter away, Tom Latham is not interested to play that.
Full again and on off, Tom Latham drives it towards short covers.
Fuller one and on middle, Tom Latham keeps it out towards short leg.
FOUR! Henry Nicholls gets off the mark with a boundary! James Anderson bowls this back of a length and outside off, Henry Nicholls stays there and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Length again and outside off again, Henry Nicholls offers no shot at it.
On a length and on off, angling away, Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
Henry Nicholls comes in at number 5.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! James Anderson gets rid of Will Young with a peach of a delivery. He lands this on a good length with the angle and in the channel outside off, nips away just a bit, Will Young tries to play at it, but the movement away takes a slight nick towards the keeper where Ben Foakes takes his third catch of this innings. Young could not have done much there as this was just perfect from James Anderson.
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Foakes b James Anderson

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller and on off, Will Young leans on and fends it to the right of gully.
This is on a good length and on middle, angling in, Will Young defends it towards short leg.
It will be James Anderson to steam in from the other end. He has been right on the money so far. A stern test for the Kiwi batters await.
Touch fuller and outside off, Tom Latham leaves it alone.
On a length and on off, Tom Latham knocks it towards short covers.
Pitched up, on leg, Tom Latham clips it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Fine shot! Stuart Broad serves a hafl-volley, outside off, Tom Latham shows the full face of the bat to drive it through covers for a beautiful boundary.
Full again and around off, Tom Latham drills it through cover-point for a brace.
Full and on off, Will Young pushes it towards covers for a single.

The post-Lunch session is set to begin. The English players make their way out on the middle and take the field. Followed by Tom Latham and Will Young who walk out with their swords. It will be Stuart Broad to start with the ball now. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

England are dictating the Test match here. First, Ben Stokes makes a solid call to declare the innings at 435 runs, it also came after Joe Root made his 150 runs. In spite of losing wickets at regular intervals earlier in the morning session, England cruised along really well and racked up 120 runs. Later on, with the new ball in hand, James Anderson continued on his merry way. After becoming the number 1 Test bowler, James Anderson did not waste time to get into the wicket's column here as he struck in his very first over. Soon, he added one more to his tally and the hosts are certainly on the back foot here. The post-Lunch session would be very crucial for the Kiwis. Will they be able to provide with a solid counter-punch. To find out, do join us at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT).

New Zealand are off to a horrendous start with the bat. They lost 2 wickets in the 7 overs that they batted so far. Tom Latham seems to be in good touch so far. Will Young is comparatively new at the crease and would be hoping to stick around for long. The Kiwis certainly have their task cut out here. Looking at the evidence of England's innings, it was clear that the batters do struggle early on, but the conditions only get better as the day progresses. England were off to a similar start with the bat and two certain players took the momentum away from the hosts. The Kiwis though would hope their batters can step-up and give a run for their money.

It has been all about England in the morning session on Day 2, first they dominated with the bat and later challenged with the ball in hand as well. New Zealand find themselves in a spot of bother, as they are trailing by 423 runs.
Overpitched and on off, Tom Latham drives it towards short covers. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Back of a length and on middle, Tom Latham stays back and keeps it out to the leg side.
Pitched up, on middle, Tom Latham works it towards short mid-wicket.
EDGED AND FOUR! This is short of a length and outside off, Tom Latham slashes hard at it, and it goes well over the slips towards the third man fence for a boudnary.
On a length and on off, Tom Latham steers it towards gully.
Full and on middle, Will Young flicks it towards deep backward square leg for a single.
A maided over! Ollie Robinson serves this touch fuller, outside off, Tom Latham offers no shot at it.
Back of a length and outside off, angling away, Tom Latham shoulders arms to it.
BEATEN! Ollie Robinson bowls this on a hard length and just around off, angling away, Tom Latham looks to play at it, but gets beaten on the outside edge.
On a length and on middle, Tom Latham looks to defend, but gets an outside edge on the bounce towards gully.
Full again and on leg, Tom Latham works it towards short mid-wicket.
Ollie Robinson starts with a full delivery and on middle, Tom Latham blocks it down the pitch.
Ona length, on off, angling in, Will Young strides forward and looks to defend, but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is a shout for LBW, but turned down. Ben Stokes decides against the review.
Pitched up, on middle, Will Young tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
This is on a good length and on the sixth stump line, shaping in, Will Young leaves it alone.
Touch fuller and around off, Will Young lifts his bat and lets it go to the keeper.
Will Young is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! James Anderson strikes again! Kane Williamson's woes continue as he walks back for yet another low score. James Anderson this time serves this slightly fuller than the previous delivery around off, shaping away, Kane Williamson looks to push it away without any footwork and gets a thin outside edge towards the keeper where Ben Foakes makes no mistake. New Zealand two down now!
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Foakes b James Anderson

Commentary.Commentary: BEAUTY! James Anderson lands this short of a length and on off, takes off with extra bounce, Kane Williamson gets hurried and gets beaten on the outside edge as he tries to fend it.
On a length and on off, Tom Latham pushes it towards short covers, Kane Williamson wants the run, but he is sent back.
Goes back to his fuller length, on middle, Tom Latham turns it towards short leg.
Pulls his length back a bit, outside off, nips away, Tom Latham is not interested to play that.
Another full delivery, on off, Tom Latham blocks it to the off side.
Stuart Broad is struggling with his line to the left-hander here. He bowls this full again but down the leg side, Tom Latham misses his flick.
This is full and on off, Kane Williamson tries to defend it but gets an outside edge past gully, Harry Brook chases it and slides in and just manages to keep it inside. Three runs taken!
Pitched up, on off, Tom Latham pushes it towards short covers.
Overpitched and outside off, Tom Latham drives it through point for a couple of runs.
This is on a hard length in the channel outsdide off, Tom Latham leaves it alone.
On a length and on off, Tom Latham guides it towards gully.
Full again and on middle, Tom Latham knocks it back towards the bowler.
This is full and on middle, Kane Williamson looks to defend it, but gets a leading edge through point for a single and gets off the mark.
Stuart Broad strays away from his line again and serves this full but down the leg side one more time, Tom Latham lets it go to the keeper.
Stuart Broad continues with the fuller length, on middle, Tom Latham keeps it out to the leg side.
Overpitched and on middle, angling in, Tom Latham tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
Pitched up, on off, angling in, Tom Latham looks to play at it, but gets an inside edge onto his pads as the ball rolls to the off side.
Full again and down the leg again, Tom Latham misses his flick this time.
Stuart Broad begins with a full delivery but way down the leg side, Tom Latham leaves it alone.
It will be Stuart Broad to steam in from the opposite end.
On a length and on off, Kane Williamson steers it towards gully.
Kane Williamson comes in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! What a start from England! James Anderson draws first blood! He serves this touch fuller and on off,angling away this time, Devon Conway looks to defend, but the angle takes a thin outside edge towards the keeper where Ben Foakes pouches it safely. There is a stiffled appeal for caught behind, but turned down. Ben Stokes takes the review though after some discussion. UltraEdge confirms that Conway has hit it and England players are delighted. Devon Conway has to make that long walk back to the hut now without troubling the scorers.
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Foakes b James Anderson

Commentary.Commentary: Good bowling! James Anderson bowls this back of a length and on middle, shaping in sharply, Devon Conway offers no shot at it, and gets hit on his stomach area.
Full again and on middle, Devon Conway knocks it to the leg side.
Tom Latham and New Zealand are underway! This is full and on middle, Tom Latham turns it in front of short mid-wicket for a single.
James Anderson starts with a hard-length delivery, on middle, Tom Latham stays back and blocks it down the pitch.
